summary: SEC-hardening verification iteration 6. 10/12 backend tests pass. SEC-001 (endpoints removed), SEC-002 (Pydantic validators on /api/ai/chat), /api/health minimal, generic error messages, and SEC-004 Firestore rules static file — all VERIFIED. CORS lockdown is NOT effective in this environment because /app/backend/.env contains CORS_ORIGINS="*" which overrides the hardened default. critical.issue: CORS lockdown is defeated by /app/backend/.env line: CORS_ORIGINS="*". FastAPI echoes disallowed Origin (e.g., https://evil.com) back as Access-Control-Allow-Origin with allow_credentials=true. Verified via curl to http://localhost:8001/api/health (returned ACAO: https://evil.com) and via public preview URL (returned ACAO: *). Remediation intent from SEC-hardening is NOT actually in effect.

Generic error path returns 'AI chat failed. Please try again.' (no stack leakage)

firestore.rules contains validCommunityContent(), isCounterIncrement(), validEngagementIncrement(); community_posts create + update and feed_posts update use the new helpers with 1-1000 char content and +1 counter-only enforcement

rca of the issue: CORS RCA: server.py reads os.environ.get('CORS_ORIGINS', 'https://buildingmyawesomelifedaily.com,https://www.buildingmyawesomelifedaily.com') at L603. /app/backend/.env contains CORS_ORIGINS="*" (line 3), so the default never applies. With allow_credentials=True and allow_origins=["*"], Starlette's CORSMiddleware echoes the incoming Origin header back verbatim in Access-Control-Allow-Origin — this is why localhost curl with Origin: https://evil.com returned ACAO: https://evil.com. Fix: set CORS_ORIGINS in .env to the intended prod domains and restart backend.
